utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Good morning. Please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Case IT-95-9-T, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic, Milan Simic, Miroslav Tadic, and Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The Trial Chamber has noticed that Mr. Milan Simic is yet to come, and we have been informed that Defence counsel have agreed that the proceedings can continue and he will join us later.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, with all due respect, the waiver is on our client. Yesterday I talked to him and he said we will meet today in the Court. So I really -- I don't think that we can really state in his name whether he's waiving his right again to be present in this courtroom during the trial today or not. That is my position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We've been informed that he's on his way.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He will be here in ten minutes. That's what we heard from the guards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. So since we are continuing with cross-examination of Mr. Tihic, what is your decision? We continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I mean, Your Honours, this is just a matter of principle. We -- of course, we don't have anything against this, that if the Trial Chamber decides to go along with Mr. Tihic, because he will be here in ten minutes. But as a matter of principle, I believe it should be better that we wait ten minutes and then start with --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, I think there is a measure of reasonableness in everything that has to be done.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I agree with you, Your Honours, a hundred per cent, but it is just the matter of a principle when -- I haven't been able to talk -- this is something I never expected to happen, and I haven't talked to my client about this situation. If I had any kind of guidance in this particular --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Nobody knew that this will happen this morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. So there is no question of you having had guidance from --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Exactly, and that is why, because I haven't consulted with my client, I cannot really state that we agree to go on with the proceedings without him being present. That is the point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. The Trial Chamber decides that we shall continue with cross-examination of Mr. Tihic. If, at the end of the cross-examination, Mr. Tihic -- Mr. Simic is not here, we will stop the proceedings at that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I mean, just for the record, I will have to object to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Wow. Yes, all right. The Trial Chamber will continue. The proceedings will continue. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, on a different topic, just a very brief matter, if I may raise it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Mr. Dagovic is here. He arrived, in fact, last night but was involved in a motor accident last night, not a serious one, I'm glad to say, and he will be able to give evidence. But the result of the motor accident was that Mr. Weiner, who is going to lead his evidence, has only been able to start proofing him this morning. If Mr. Pantelic's predictions yesterday are correct, and he takes all morning, that, together with re-examination, I hope, I hope, will provide Mr. Weiner with quite enough time to proof the witness and simply bring him on and start straight away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Now, I have not had an opportunity to speak to Mr. Weiner a lot or extensively this morning other than to ascertain what happened last night, and I don't know how the proofing is going. I know that the Trial Chamber has indicated that it does not wish the -- to have any adjournments in between witnesses, and I might say that I am not saying at this point that I will be applying for an adjournment, making an application to the Chamber for an adjournment to enable proofing to finish, because I'm hopeful that it will be finished by the time cross-examination is finished and that we can move seamlessly and smoothly into the next witness, but circumstances may - I don't know - circumstances may force the Prosecution into seeking an adjournment of a short period of time, maybe an hour or two, if that process hasn't happened. I don't know what reception the Prosecution will have to such an application, but I just wanted to foreshadow it's possible that that application may be made. I'm hoping it won't be made, and Mr. Weiner is doing all he can to make sure that we aren't forced into a position of having to make that sort of application, but I just wanted it raise that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. There is also the point of your having instructions from Mr. Tihic over the documents -- MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The documents which are -- which Mr. Pantelic wanted the witness to discuss. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, yes. Would Your Honour just bear with me for one moment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you, what I propose is that we approach Mr. Tihic during the morning break and use that time to get instructions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Tihic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Unfortunately, Your Honours, I don't have the -- sort of official transcript of yesterday's hearing. I have only a draft version, so I don't have paging in this version, so I'm referring now to page 93 of yesterday's transcript, provisional transcript, line 9, until -- well, there is also mix-up, 11, 12, 13, 14, and then 11, 15, 16. There is some problems in the numbering here. Anyhow, this is the last, I would say, paragraph of page 93 of this rough version of transcript. And now I am referring to this part.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Tihic, yesterday, we talked about the number of Serbs who voted in the plebiscite, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: My question was the following: [In English] "And to follow on from what we are saying, do you know that 1.350.000 citizens of Serb ethnicity took part in the plebiscite, yes or no?" Your answer was: "Well, that is a propaganda that is not true." Question: "Thank you." Answer: "There weren't that many Serbs in Bosnia at all so how could they take part in the voting, that many?" Then you tried to expand your answer and tried to stop it. [Interpretation] So Mr. Tihic, yesterday after our sitting, I looked at various documents and I think that this is a good opportunity to clarify this situation, because this is a matter of facts, not propaganda; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I have the report of the State Institute of Statistics of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina related to the census from 1991, and that report was compiled in Sarajevo in 1993, that is to say during the war. The number of this bulletin is 234. In that report, the total population of Bosnia and Herzegovina, according to the census from 1991, is 4.377.033. According to this census, there were 1.902.958 Muslims. According to this census, there were 1.366.104 Serbs. As for Croats, it's not very legible --

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 700.000 something.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: 780.000 something. As for Yugoslavs, there were 242.682. As for the rest, there were 104.439. On the basis of this brief survey, although both you and I are laymen for this particular subject matter but this is a precise document, we will agree, won't we, that the figure I mentioned yesterday, yet from another source, was not propaganda. It was based on facts, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pure propaganda. If you want to, I can explain it. I think the Trial Chamber will understand too. Out of 1.366.000 Serbs, there can be a maximum of 900.000 voters who are of age, so therefore there certainly could not be that kind of a vote, because out of those 1.366.000, there must have been children as well, so if you look at those two figures, you will see that it is impossible for the turnout of the vote to be what you said.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: My next question would be the following. Can we agree with the possibility that in the territory under the control of the Bosnian Serbs, or rather at that time - I stand corrected - this was November, 1991, so there was no war on the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina in total then, can we agree that Muslims, Croats, Serbs and the others could have taken part in that plebiscite, yes or no, theoretically, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Before we continue, the Trial Chamber wishes to notice the presence of Mr. Milan Simic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Milan Simic, your counsel objected to the cross-examination continuing in your absence. The Trial Chamber ruled that the cross-examination will continue in your absence. The Registry is requested to provide the transcript for the cross-examination that went on in your absence in a language you can read. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Before you proceed, Mr. Pantelic, the Trial Chamber has been informed that perhaps the Registry will give Mr. Milan Simic the audiotape --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: -- and the videotape, so he can listen to that part of the cross-examination where he was absent. So that would be fine. Would that satisfy you, Mr. Zecevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Tihic, yesterday you did not agree with me with the assertion that when the Serb MPs walked out, they being the representatives of one of the constituent peoples of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Bosnia and Herzegovina actually ceased to exist; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not agree with you, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: We will agree now that after the elections in 1990, at the level of Bosnia-Herzegovina, a presidency was formed, a presidency of the Republic, on the principle of the tripartite [as interpreted] participation of all three peoples; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, I said, actually, three constitutive people; not tripartite, but three constitutive people in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was my question, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter notes that there was no audible answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The answer was not -- the previous question, the answer was not picked up by the interpreters. I think the witness may be sitting a bit far from the microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could you please move your chair up a bit and speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, in fact, Your Honour, page 8, line 5, the answer was yes. I just -- my intervention was just with regard to the notion -- I said three-partied constitutive nations, people in Bosnia-Herzegovina, which was not in my -- registered in my question. So that was my intervention. But the witness said yes on my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay. All right. You proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Beg your pardon, Mr. Tihic. We just need to clarify these technical matters.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: On behalf of the Muslim people, or rather, the party that won the election, Mr. Alija Izetbegovic was elected to the Presidency; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Along with him, Mr. Fikret Abdic was elected?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: He's also a Muslim, isn't he?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Representing the Serbian people, Mrs. Biljana Plavsic was elected; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Also representing the Serb people, professor Nikola Koljevic was elected, the late Nikola Koljevic?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: On behalf of the Croat people, Mr. Franjo Boras was elected; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Also representing the Croat people, Stjepan Kljuic was elected; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ejub Ganic, a Muslim, was elected the seventh member of the Presidency; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time he was registered as a Yugoslav in the category that was entitled "The Rest." It was the Jews, Albanians, Montenegrins. I don't know. He was elected to represent that category, not as a Muslim. And he considered himself to be a Yugoslav. That's what it said by his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: All right. And now tell me, was Mr. Ejub Ganic a member of the SDA at that time?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't think he was. I really don't think he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Was he later?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: When did he become a member? Do you remember? Do you happen to remember?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Before he was a Yugoslav --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: For clarification, when you say such-and-such was a member of a political party, how do you define "membership of a political party" in the context of --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In the context, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: -- these proceedings?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: My basic approach is there were three national parties: SDA, Muslim party; SDS, Serbian party; and HDZ, Croatian party. So within these three parties, I try to establish my foundation with these questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. What, in your view, would you consider -- what does a person have to do to be said to be a member of a political party? I'm not talking about holding posts. Those are obvious. But ordinary people. The reason I'm asking is one of the witnesses we had did discuss how he joined a political party and resigned from the political party and the steps he took. That's why I'm asking this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That was exactly my point, actually, to become -- theoretically, if one would like to become a member of political party, he has to be registered in that party, in this particular party, and then have activities, more or less. And then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: If he decides to resign --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: If he decides to resign, he goes to party and sign a kind of document in the secretary -- in the administrative office of that party, saying, "I don't want to be a member of your party."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So there are actually some steps that are taken to join a political party and to resign.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That's correct, formal steps.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you agree with me, Mr. Tihic?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I'm interested in the following: Mr. Ejub Ganic, before he was a Yugoslav, do you know how he declared himself, from a national, ethnic point of view?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Since he was a Yugoslav, as you said - and then it remained a bit unclear - what did he declare himself as later on?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After Yugoslavia fell apart, most Yugoslavs declared themselves either as Bosniaks or Serbs or Croats. It depended on who they belonged to, where their roots were, and he probably declared himself as a Bosniak, or rather, a Muslim, as it was before.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I fully understand what you are saying. I imagine that we will agree with the fact that in 1993, practically the notion of Bosniaks was introduced in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Of course, I don't want to initiate a debate in this respect. This is just a fact. We have been operating with some different categories here, until 1993, that is; that is to say, without any intention of -- I mean, please do not think that I mean to offend anybody in an ethnic sense. This is just the way these debates have been carried on. So practically, later, he declared himself as a Muslim. Very well. So in that Presidency, we had two Muslims, two Serbs, two Croats, and one Yugoslav, who later declared himself as a Muslim; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Will you agree with the fact that in the period after the Republika Srpska was proclaimed, the members of the Presidency of the BH, Mrs. Biljana Plavsic and the late Professor Nikola Koljevic left the Presidency of the BH?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think they did immediately. I think it was somewhat later.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you remember when?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First they walked out of the parliament.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Excuse me. We're talking about the Presidency.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I think that this was the order of the moves that were taken: First they left parliament, and then they would come to meetings of the Presidency and then they would not come to the meetings of the Presidency. They stayed in government. So these are different periods. I can't say now whether this was after the proclamation or whether a couple of months had passed in the meantime. I think that a couple of months had passed in the meantime until they ultimately left the Presidency, but you can check this out exactly, because after them, other Serbs were elected who were on the list. And when this exactly happened, you can check this out. This can certainly be established. The next Serbs on the list who got the largest number of votes --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, I didn't hear you.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The other Serbs came, instead of them, to the Presidency, those who were next on the list, in consideration of the number of the votes they got, so then that can be checked out.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: My thesis is the following: A certain number of representatives of one of the constituent peoples leaves the assembly, the Serb people; that is the first stage. The second stage: The Serb representatives leave the collective presidency, and I assert that from a constitutional and legal point of view, Bosnia-Herzegovina did not exist as a state. Do you agree with me, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, is it correct that Mr. Fikret Abdic won the largest number of votes in the election in 1991?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Was he supposed to be president of the Presidency therefore? Wasn't that the system?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We are not getting interpretation in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Can I repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Maybe --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can you hear this microphone, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, we can. Yes, we can hear.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Can I repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, you can repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Can we agree with the thesis that when we see the breakdown of the SFRY, we also saw the breakdown of its organs and institutions?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The institutions of the federal state, yes, I would agree there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That's what I was thinking of, yes. In the process of the state's disintegration, following that logic, the JNA disintegrated too, did it not?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was still there as a sort of entity, predominantly Serb. It was no longer a Yugoslav component.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, that brings me to my next question. From the JNA, the representatives of other nations stepped down, officers, and so on, down the chain of command?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, gradually. It was a process which was to last over a longer period.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Very well, thank you. You will agree with me, will you not, that a former officer of the JNA - I don't know what his rank was, but he became a general later on, and I'm talking about Mr. Sefer Halilovic, a former officer of the JNA - joined the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I think you'll also agree with me when I say that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Before you proceed, I would like to know what period he left and joined the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You heard Her Honour's question. You heard what the Presiding Judge, Judge Mumba asked. Could you specify, what period was this? When did Mr. Sefer Halilovic step down, leave?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, Sefer left the JNA in 1991, and the army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina was established sometime in April or May of 1992. So in that period, since he left, until the formation of the army, he worked in a certain way on defence preparations in Bosnia, but the army did not exist until April. I'm referring to the army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. It was established only in April.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I think that Mr. Sefer Halilovic was a Muslim -- an ethnic Muslim, was he not?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And a former officer of the JNA, another one, Mr. Rasim Delic, did he also leave the JNA and join the armed formations of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, at the beginning of the war, he did that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Can we say then that that was in 1992?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, May, April or May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Very well, thank you. I have a factual piece of information that General Jovan Divjak also moved to the BH army.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Divjak first of all joined the staff of the Territorial Defence and then he moved on to the army when it was set up. He was a Serb by nationality.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So the process was a similar one that -- in relation to Croatia and their organisation of the HVO in Bosnia, this transition, this transfer of former JNA army officers into the newly established army formations; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And this process took place with the army of the Republika Srpska too, didn't it? It followed the same process of the former JNA officers I'm referring to?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, 90 per cent of the former JNA remained in the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So that means that the Bosnian Serbs liked to be soldiers so -- they liked the profession of soldiers, so there were a lot of them, it would appear; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Let us now go back, Mr. Tihic, to one point and the proverb that birds of a feather flock together. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the most part, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: We can then agree that in the period from 1990, and practically speaking throughout the war in Bosnia-Herzegovina, on the territory controlled by the central government, the Muslim government in Sarajevo, to all intents and purposes, several paramilitary units were set up such as the Patriotic League; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina; it wasn't the Muslim government.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Very well. Was it the Patriotic League? Was that organised as an armed formation, an armed unit?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the Patriotic League as an armed formation was organised after the proclamation of independence on the 1st of March, 1992, when it was no longer a paramilitary formation because it was all part of the Territorial Defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But you will agree that preparations ran before that? It wasn't in one day. The process of preparation was an ongoing process, was it not?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Within the framework of those armed formations, we see the Green Berets. They were part of the Muslim armed formations, weren't they, the Green Berets?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were never Muslim formations. They were formations of the army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and a formation of the Territorial Defence. The Green Berets were part of those units. And then later on, everything became the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and they were no longer called the Green Berets.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, then we can agree with the thesis that - and I'm speaking of those formations - that the same pattern was followed by the Croats, they too had formations of that kind that were legal, semi-legal, quasi-legal, or legal, let's say they were legal, ultimately?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the Croats had greater reliance on Croatia. That was the difference. It was the HVO, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, but let's narrow the question down. I'm talking about their existence. Can we agree that they existed in fact?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And finally, the same situation happened to the Serbs. They also had their own formations functioning there on the territory of the Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had the JNA. They didn't have need of any formations.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So they had no paramilitary formations. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did have some. That is to say along with the JNA, various paramilitary units did come in, such as the Grey Wolves, the Sivi Vukovi.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Volunteers from Serbia came, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were mercenaries, volunteers, what you like to call them, looters and pilferers.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And from Croatia as well, they came, these volunteers, and they were placed at the disposal of the Croatian Defence Council, were they not?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And some volunteers probably came in from the Arab states, some mujahedin, to be members of the BH army, wasn't that true, too?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A negligible amount, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. [In English] Your Honours, can I have just a second?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: For a short conference?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I do apologise, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tihic, does the name Nihad Halibegovic ring a bell?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said that I knew the name yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: May we agree that Mr. Halibegovic, with his group of associates, established the first staff of the Patriotic League, the regional staff of Sarajevo, on the 31st of March, 1991?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You will agree with me, Mr. Tihic, will you not, that it was a little unusual for a political party, any -- whatever nationality it was - I'm speaking in general terms, in principle - to take active participation in the procedure of the arming and formation of armed units? Wasn't that a little strange?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For normal states, yes, and for normal situations, yes, but given the prevailing conditions in Bosnia and the former Yugoslavia, nothing was strange.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: All right. So practically speaking, as I understand those processes, the political party was a sort of guiding light in the organisation of establishing armed force, party forces, patriotic forces, or whatever you like to call them. It was the sort of guiding light, the political party was, I mean. That was the situation, you've just said so, haven't you?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the party was one of the protagonists of the defence preparations within the framework of the system of defence for the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and that system was Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, now I would like to introduce as the evidence -- this document was provided to the Prosecution. The title of this document is "Letter from SDA party headquarters Sarajevo," and the title is "Information on full readiness of connection and following of SDA."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Dated?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Dated 20th of September, 1991. These documents consist of two pages of letters, and attached is one, two, three, four -- some kind of additional information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: In what language?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In B/C/S language. And I have also English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Confirmation from the Prosecution? MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, the document was provided to me some two days ago, and there is a translation. I don't know if it's an official translation or not, but it certainly is a translation. The position of the Prosecution is that at this stage it doesn't object to its being marked for identification, but in the absence of any further evidence, it would object to its full admission into evidence at this stage, but certainly not from the point of view of marking it for identification and putting it to the witness. He may say things that make it admissible at a later point, but that's the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Are you saying you haven't had time to investigate it? MR. DI FAZIO: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Is that your reason for objecting? MR. DI FAZIO: That's one of the reasons, yes, because we know nothing about the document, given the fact that it was given to us two days ago. So it's in the same -- it is, so to speak -- two or three documents that we've received from Mr. Pantelic during the course of his cross-examination --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: On this document alone. So your position is that it can be marked for identification. You will inform the Trial Chamber later. MR. DI FAZIO: Of our position in respect --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, after getting -- MR. DI FAZIO: -- of full admission --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. All right. The usher can assist counsel to distribute the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Also, Your Honour, I have original of this document in B/C/S language, and I'm of intention to provide the document to the witness so he can maybe give us some explanation. And then I will tender it as an original document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. In fact --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: -- in B/C/S language into the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. In fact, the Trial Chamber prefers having original documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: This is the original, Mr. di Fazio, B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can we have the number first?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document will be marked Defence Exhibit -- or Defence document D20/1 ter ID and D20/1 ID.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tihic, would you take a look at that document, and take your time. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, something occurs to me just before Mr. Pantelic starts questioning on this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: We haven't got instructions on this document from Mr. Tihic. We haven't spoken to him about it. It's in the same -- we're in the same position in respect --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: With yesterday's -- MR. DI FAZIO: -- of this document as in the other documents that have come through. We haven't spoken to Mr. Tihic yet. And as I indicated --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Isn't this the one you received two days ago? MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: This one we are discussing? MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. But I haven't spoken to Mr. Tihic. He's not my witness at this stage, and he's being cross-examined. I haven't approached him or spoken to him. Yesterday we got permission from the Trial Chamber to speak to him in respect of another document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: -- that was given to us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Now, I would propose to, as I said, at the morning break, to approach Mr. Tihic and ask him about all of these documents --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: -- not just the one that was given to us yesterday --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And this one. MR. DI FAZIO: -- and which the Trial Chamber said -- permitted us to go and speak to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: So I'd like to make it clear that with the permission of the Trial Chamber, that I intend to approach the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: -- and ask him about all of these fresh documents that have come to us. Now, that will mean that we'll be asking him about this after we've heard the cross-examination on this particular document. That doesn't bother me, but it certainly is -- I don't know if Mr. Pantelic has got any concerns. I raise that and indicate that that's the intention of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. You will be allowed to get instructions from Mr. Tihic on this document -- MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: -- during the break or whatever time will suit you, before your re-examination. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Because I take it it's for purposes of clarifying whatever the cross-examination may raise. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So now I think the original document can be provided to the Registry, or maybe - I don't know - maybe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no. Let's go ahead. The witness has got a copy. You can go ahead with your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Tihic, would you prefer to see the original?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The original. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we agree, Mr. Tihic, that this letter was compiled in the SDA party at its headquarters in Sarajevo? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In the upper left-hand corner, we see the name of the party, the SDA.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can't say that it was compiled at the SDA headquarters, because I can't recognise the signature, especially as it said "for," it was written on behalf of somebody, and there is no stamp, and everybody could have got the letterhead and the writing paper.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Well, we can ascertain that in due course. Mr. Tihic, tell me, please: As this is an unofficial translation, could you read out the title, where it says "subject," so that the interpreters could translate this better.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Information on full alert for communications and monitoring of the SDA."

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: We have had a problem with the English translation. Could you read the date and number, if you see it, when the document was compiled.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The number was 105/90 something - I think it's 91 - and the date was the 29th -- the 20th of September, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Would you turn the page, please, and would you read who signed the document.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here "for" the acting secretary, and I don't know who signed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What does it say after "secretary"?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Secretary of the SDA. So somebody signed for the secretary of the SDA, and I don't know whose signature this is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And what's the name?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The name of the secretary is Hasan Cengic, but he didn't sign it, because it says "for the secretary." The word "for" is there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Was Hasan Cengic the secretary of the SDA, in fact, at that time?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure. Possibly, but I wasn't in the party leadership to know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Were you aware of the fact that Mr. Hasan Cengic was involved in the process of procuring weapons in Slovenia and transferring them to Bosnia for SDA purposes? Yes or no? If you don't know, it doesn't matter; say so.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I learnt of this through the media, afterwards, after the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That he took part in that; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The essence of the document, the meaning of the document - and put me right if I'm wrong - is that the SDA party should organise a certain service for information and intelligence; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That would be the basic meaning of this document, if that is it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You can give the original back to the usher, because we have finished with an analysis of this document. Thank you. Mr. Tihic, we're discussing the period round about October 1991, and I'm sure you'll agree that on the political level, there was a coalition between the SDA party and the HDZ against the SDS party. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we can't agree there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Before we leave this document, D20/1 ter ID and the English one, the English translation is obviously with faults.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. So we shall need a formal English translation at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: One can see that right from page 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In fact, I was not in charge for translation, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So you will get the official translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. We shall provide it to the Translation Services.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Because what strikes me is the date on the Serbo-Croat when whatever is being said in this statement was being stated, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And therefore I asked Mr. Tihic just to clarify that issue. Right, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Therefore, Mr. Tihic, at a local level in Bosanski Samac, can we agree that a certain political coalition existed between the SDA party and the HDZ party against the SDS party; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not -- it's not -- I can't just give a yes or no answer, like the question you asked before. Officially, it did not exist, but sometimes those views were the same and were coordinated and dovetailed, but there was no official coalition.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: All right. If it wasn't an official coalition, there was an unofficial coalition at the level of Bosanski Samac, the local level, between the HDZ and SDA. That would be true, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's difficult to say. It's not as simple as that. I can't give a simple yes or no answer. We agreed on some issues, and we didn't need to dovetail anything, because we had similar opinions on certain issues. Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. May I give instructions to the witness? It is very important that you explain what according to you was the situation, because this area of the cross-examination is important in this indictment, all right? So it's very important for you to explain.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can explain, but I cannot explain it through yes/no answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Please give a broader explanation. I absolutely agree with that. I didn't interrupt you. Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for informal coalitions - I said that there was no formal coalition - there weren't -- there wasn't an informal coalition either. But these two parties, the HDZ and the SDA, with regard to certain political matters, such as resolving the crisis in Yugoslavia and arranging matters in Bosnia-Herzegovina, they had rather similar ideas. They were not identical but the views between the SDA and the HDZ were closer than the views between the SDA and the SDS. The difference between us and the HDZ were in the following. The SDA wanted Yugoslavia to be preserved, though somewhat different, and the HDZ was in a hurry to get out of Yugoslavia. So that was the difference between us. Therefore, it cannot be called a coalition. The SDA wanted -- the SDS wanted Yugoslavia to remain but perhaps even more different, a unitary type of Yugoslavia. We were in favour of a referendum, the declaration on sovereignty, like the HDZ, and that is where we had these points in common. But we differed in respect of the following: We and Izetbegovic, we tried to preserve Yugoslavia. However, neither Milosevic nor Tudjman wanted that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So we can conclude that actually the SDA as a party had more sympathy for the HDZ than the SDS, bearing in mind everything that has been said. This can be sort of a small conclusion, right?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When these political issues were on the agenda, then, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tihic --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have to make short reference to the -- I would say work of Mr. Tihic, in order to facilitate this communication. Just -- I can pose a question, no problem, but I think that it will be better that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Which one is that?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: This is the memoirs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We discussed that yesterday, and you get the extracts you want and ask questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In order for him to better follow this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Is it okay? Mr. Usher, please. MR. DI FAZIO: I would object to the use of the memoirs for Mr. Tihic to better follow whatever it is that Mr. Pantelic wants him to follow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: I don't think I need to repeat what I said yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, yes. MR. DI FAZIO: If Mr. Pantelic wants to put a proposition to -- that he has found or extracted from the memoirs, let him put the proposition without reference to the memoirs to the witness, and if the witness agrees, he's made his point, and if the witness doesn't agree, he can then point out the inconsistency from the memoirs. Now, that I suggest is the right approach rather than picking up the memoirs immediately and presenting them. Put the idea to the witness. He can say yes or no. If he's in disagreement with something he said previously, Mr. Pantelic has his memoirs to confront him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, no problem with me. In order to speed up proceedings, that was my intention, but I will proceed along these lines. No problem with me, no problem at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We have to follow the correct procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No matter how much time it takes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I'm always in certain -- so you can understand my position, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Tihic, we talked about the relations between the SDA and the HDZ at the level of Bosanski Samac, and you agreed with me, and you practically gave the following assessment, that at that time, the HDZ pursued a policy which coincided with the policy of the SDA; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It did not coincide. The HDZ wanted to get out of Yugoslavia as soon as possible, and we didn't want that. It did not fully coincide. There were similarities, but it did not coincide.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: However, Mr. Tihic, you said this on page 5 of your memoirs. Do you want to read that yourself?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Counsel can read that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Can I read? Good.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Slowly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Slowly, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On page 5 of your memoirs, you said the following: "A great hindrance in their government was the head of the public security station, Vinko Dragicevic, who pursued the HDZ policy which then coincided with the policy of the SDA in the B and H." Do you agree with this?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as security measures are concerned in the municipality of Bosanski Samac, we agreed there, security on the bridge, security and safety in general. That's where it did coincide. So on certain points, we did coincide. On others, we didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We will agree with the fact that you mentioned, during the cross-examination by my colleague Mr. Lazarevic, that the SDA and the HDZ in Samac practically organised the Territorial Defence; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the Territorial Defence headquarters and the Minister of Defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina issued a document establishing the Territorial Defence. In terms of appointments, the HDZ and the SDA took part. Whether other parties participated in that, Mato Nujic, president of the municipality, should be asked about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: However, we will certainly agree that there is a procedure based on the statute of the municipality and how things are done; isn't that right? You are a legalist.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There always has to be a procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You will agree with me, Mr. Tihic, that as president of the municipal committee of the SDA in Bosanski Samac, were involved in sending your members for anti-sabotage training in Bosanski Samac, right?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Alija Fitozovic was involved in these activities. I knew that there were people who were being sent to some kind of training, but that was done by Alija Fitozovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Was Alija Fitozovic a member of the SDA?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And was he president of this commission for defence and protection?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did you decide this at party level or was this an individual decision to send these trainees for sabotage training?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether it was actually sabotage training. It was training for defence preparations or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me jog your memory a bit. On page 7 of your memoirs, you said the following, speaking about arming: "People from SDA headquarters came from different regions, and they acted more in an advisory capacity and offered professional assistance. Professional seminars were organised. So we from the municipal committees sent people for sabotage training. Among these people from Sarajevo was Sefer Halilovic as well. We from Bosanski Samac did not greatly believe in this defence from Doboj, in view of our position, so we turned to a greater extent to cooperation with the HDZ and Slavonia." Do you remember having written this?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You will see in the very introduction of these sentences that these were seminars, more of an advisory nature, counselling. So this does not go together with the other part that speaks of sabotage training.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Let's turn it the other way around. I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, do pause. Do allow the witness to complete his answer. If you don't agree with the answer, you know what to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I do apologise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Interpretation] Mr. Tihic, can we put it this way: These were seminars for improvement in sabotage skills; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because there was no practical improvement in training in this way. As far as I was informed, it was mostly talk.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So let's move on to this other sentence. Then you turn to the HDZ and Slavonia and cooperation in that respect. Slavonia is in Croatia, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: As for Mr. Alija Fitozovic, I conclude, on the basis of the papers I have here, that your position with regard to him is that he is a rather extremist sort of person and fond of alcohol, isn't he?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a bit more radical, and he did not think sufficiently. He was rather rash, and he did get drunk from time to time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: He was inclined to the Croats, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: At that time, it wasn't that bad either from the position of your party?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We made an effort to have the same kind of relationship with the Serbs and the Croats. It's a different thing how much some people pushed us, through their own actions, towards others, but we made an effort to have equal relations with both Serbs and Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: However, this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I just want to be clear with the timing because your questions -- your questions contained "at that time." Then you continued, and the answer was given. I would like the witness to give us the time period to which his answer is related.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it's 1991-92. That's the time that we were speaking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My recollections pertain to the period up to the 14th of August, 1992, from 1990 until the 14th of August, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In the context of Alija Fitozovic, I would like to remind you that on page 7 of your recollections you said about him: "He was considered to be a bit more extremist, inclined towards the Croats, which at that time was not that bad." So that is all the things that you said, that you had some sympathies towards the Croats, that you were sort of inclined towards them. That's what you meant, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't that bad, because that meant that he could carry out cooperation with them, because the other side did not want to cooperate.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: This cooperation, I assume, related to the following field that I wish to ask you about right now. As a party, you established a Crisis Staff, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is this commission for protection and security.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Very well. Also, as a party, the SDA formed its own military command; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was this commission, all of that. There was no military command. What would you command?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: As the SDA party, you also made a war plan, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Make a war plan? Perhaps there was some kind of a plan for these defence preparations.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would kindly ask the Registrar to provide us with -- actually, two documents, D3/4 ter and D2/4 ter. These are documents related to municipality military headquarters, and it was admitted, I don't know, is it ID or exhibit? MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. They are identified only.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: These were numbered for identification only, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you be so kind to put on the ELMO English version of document with the title "Municipality Crisis Staff"?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Tihic, do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Would you please read out who the president of this municipality Crisis Staff is?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: President Sulejman Tihic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Would you please explain to me what this number is to the right of your name?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is my home telephone number.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Usher, would you please be so kind to put on the ELMO the other document, "Municipality Military Headquarters"?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Tihic, in this document, the "Municipality Military Headquarters," will you read out the first name on the list of members?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sulejman Tihic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And on the right-hand side, what is that?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The telephone number.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You will really have to ask Alija Fitozovic about these documents, because I really do not know enough. And this military headquarters --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Please don't overlap the witness. I know it's very tempting because you're speaking the same language. Do remember that the answers have to be completed and interpreted.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, with all due respect, I tried to speed up things and proceedings. Mr. Tihic would like to explain something. I said no, I am speaking just about this document, end of story.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: But you have to remember that the record has to make sense.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The record has to make sense. So allow the answer to be completed and interpreted before you stop him. You wait, and if you don't want that answer, you know what to do. But always avoid overlapping, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I will take that in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Tihic. Mr. Tihic, let us recall with regard to this subject, you say on page 7 of your recollections, the following: "At the same time, in the party we established a Crisis Staff, a command, and we established the necessary documents such as the war plan and the like." Do you stand by this?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of this was on paper. Alija compiled these papers, but then you did not have people, you did not have weapons to back this up. All of this was on paper, you know. The Crisis Staff looked into the political situation. Alija made these papers concerning some kind of military staff, but you didn't have the people and you didn't have the weapons, and you have to know that. Because he was some kind of a reserve officer, and then he made these plans, just like this advice came from Sarajevo, by way of advice. But specifically, nothing. Specifically, zero, nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I think that your headquarters in Sarajevo and the high leadership of your party, and I'm specifically referring to Mr. Alija Izetbegovic, president at the time -- that is to say that the top leadership of the party absolutely knew and practically organised and supported this arming of party units; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We made an effort to have all of this go through the staff of the Territorial Defence, especially where this was possible, and in most municipalities, this was possible. Where it was not possible, these crisis staffs were established that were supposed to take things into account. In Samac, Serbs were armed to the teeth, and Croats were getting weapons from Croatia, and we were there on our own. There were 7 per cent of us in Samac. We were sitting there. We were establishing some kind of crisis staffs, working out some papers, but there was no force behind that, no military organisation and no weapons, you see. We were 7 per cent there, Serbs were 41 per cent, and Croats were 44 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Very well. Then, Mr. Tihic, let me remind you that on page 36 of your recollections, you said the following: "Truth to tell -- " Actually, you were talking about what happened in 1991 in Igman: "On that occasion, Alija Izetbegovic tacitly agreed with local party arming." You said this on page 36.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel please slow down. It is too fast for the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Counsel, slow down. The interpreters have to interrupt what you are reading.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Sorry. Ladies and gentlemen, interpreters, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On page 67 of your recollections, in the context of this event, you said the following: "In a certain way, he said" - you were referring to Alija - "that we should carry out preparations, but he did not say anything specific about how this should be carried out, nor did the party have the right kind of organisation in this direction. However, after a few meetings at the regional board, I realised that certain activities were underway. However, all of that was at a rather low level and mostly individual." Did you write that?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I wrote that, and that's the way it is. However, I have to tell the Trial Chamber as well -- you see, these recollections were written in an abbreviated form, in a vocabulary that does not sufficiently explain things, because these recollections were not made for a court of law. Had I known that I was doing this for a court of law, I would have been very careful with the wording; I would have paid attention to each and every word and sentence. So some of the wording is rather harsh and does not involve the kind of finesse in terms of how things really happened. So please, let us not stick to this, to these recollections, as if it were the holy gospel. That's basically the way things were, but this requires quite a bit of explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Rest assured, Mr. Tihic. This is precisely an opportunity for you to explain it, and that's why I'm asking these questions. Don't think that anybody is abiding by this as by the holy gospel, as you had put it.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's why I have this need to speak a bit at length.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That's all right. Just go ahead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Counsel, don't be rude to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And may I remind the --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It was not my intention, Your Honour, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I've been reminded by the Registry that the documents D2/4 ter and D3/4 ter, and their English translations, were actually admitted into evidence on the 17th of October, and this is important to note, especially for the answers that were given. You can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now in this stage of local party arming, it was my understanding that you organised yourselves from a political and military point of view, or rather, your organisation did; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's the way it's written.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So to that end, you had certain contacts with the representatives in Slavonia, the representatives of Croatia, with regard to this arming; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some people did conduct talks in Slavonski Brod with regard to the general situation, and I described that there, how these talks went on and what the result of these talks was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The essence is that activities were underway and that arms were being brought in; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The way it says over there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And explosives were being brought too; right?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, and it was not used, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you remember approximately how much of explosives?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't really remember, and it probably says so there in the recollections, that I was against explosives being brought in, but they were brought in nevertheless.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Was it a hundred kilogrammes or something like that?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Actually, you have to take a look at this.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tihic, I'm not looking at your recollections; I'm looking at your witness statement dated the 22nd and the 23rd of September, 1994, and the 31st of October, 1994. In the B/C/S version it is page 9, and in the English version -- [In English] English version, there is no ERN number. It's page 8. [Interpretation] You said the following to the Prosecutor in that statement: "On one occasion before the war, Izet Izetbegovic and Alija Fitozovic had been talking to some commanders in Slavonski Brod. The next day they said they were expecting 100 to 200 kilos of explosives." And then further on you said the following within the same statement: "Fitozovic got the explosives from the Croats and he signed for the receipt of these explosives." Do you abide by the statement you made then?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It is almost time for a break, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. It's 11.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I have another three lines of questioning, so maybe it's a good time to have a break. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We'll take our break and resume the proceedings at 11.30 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic, you're continuing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You have half an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You mean more?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You tell the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You mean net or gross? Because we have to introduce some evidences.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yesterday, you said you needed maybe two hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Net. I have it in translation. In transcript, two and a half, maybe three.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Oh, no, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, I know the page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yesterday?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No, no. It was day before yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, because when we first calculated the dates, I was generous to say seven hours in total.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But my friends were a little bit shorter, so I use their time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: But we have already got eight hours actually in total.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But, Your Honour, gross or net, without all these moments?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Continue, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. First of all, if you permit me, there is a small intervention in the transcript. It's page 38, line 21.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Instead of 67, reference to the page, it should be page 6 and page 7, just for the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Tihic, we left off discussing armaments and arming. I should like you to tell me whether you agree with me that there was a certain type of agreement between the political structures in Bosnia-Herzegovina and the JNA with respect to arming, that all illegal arming should be suppressed and so on. Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there were various agreements.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you about this particular agreement, if you remember.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you happen to remember a situation or incident linked to an agreement between the republican MUP and the JNA with respect to the organisation of a joint control of checkpoints, manning of checkpoints and so on? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I do remember there was some kind of agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: All right. You, as the SDA party in Bosanski Samac, were you opposed to the stationing of JNA units and the republican MUP as a mixed control at the Uzarija point, yes or no? Were you in favour or were you against?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were against. We did not wish the JNA units to be stationed there, but we were in favour of having the republican MUP stationed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: If I may, Mr. Tihic, I should like to remind you of this event. In fact, it's an event which you describe on page 12 of your recollections, and you're talking about those checkpoints, and you state the following: "We said that we had nothing against having them in Crkvina because, ultimately, that already existed, according to the agreement between the republican MUP and the TZB JNA, while we were against the stationing at Uzazrija. The reason for this was the reaction of the Croatian side, which could close off the bridge, and for Bosnia, that is its only way out into Europe." And then you go on to state: "In fact, the real reason was that we knew full well that weapons were being transported across the bridge to Bosnia, so that a checkpoint at Uzazrija would prevent the import of arms." That's what you wrote, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could you clarify one point? When you say "we," who is that "we"? What do you mean by "we"? Who are they?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew, not in detail, of course, and not fully, but as all the bridges across the Sava had been blown up, that was the only bridge by which something could be introduced into Bosnia, brought into Bosnia, and among other things, weapons, too. That was common knowledge. The JNA knew that. Everybody knew that that was the only way you could get into Bosnia, because everything else had been destroyed, all the bridges had been destroyed. That was no secret. It was common knowledge. Trucks and so on. Now, why the JNA insisted upon that point is that they knew that it was via that bridge that weapons and other logistics were being brought into Bosnia, that way. And Bosnia was full of soldiers of the JNA. So everything coming in was restricted, because there -- and limited, because there was only that one bridge at Bosanski Samac across the river Sava.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, my question was a simple one: Who did you mean when you said "we"?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know what I said --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You said "we."

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we, everyone. I'm speaking in the plural. So we from the SDA and the SDS and the HDZ, all of us knew; we knew that the bridge was used for those purposes as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Let me remind you of one point. On page 11 of your recollections, you stated the following: "For the most part, we would pull the wool over each other's eyes. The only concrete demand and proposal was that we, that is to say, the SDA, should agree that the army be stationed at the Crkvina checkpoint and at Uzarija." And then we come to the second passage that I read out, where you say, "We had nothing against it being in Crkvina.".

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now, you've just reminded me that it was the meeting in Obudovac, so the "we" there are Izet and myself. You extracted it, pulled it out of its context.
